Monday-Friday 8am-4:30pm

Summary:

The Data Scientist within the Surgery Research Enterprise at Akron Children's Hospital plays a pivotal role in advancing the department's research and analytics capabilities. Reporting to the Director of Research, the position is integral to the Surgery Research Enterprise and supports clinical research, outcomes research, and advanced analytics across surgical divisions. The Data Scientist is expected to work independently, collaborate with investigators, and develop and lead research and data science projects from concept through analysis and dissemination.

Responsibilities:

1. Supports the development of advanced analytics and data science capabilities within the Surgery Research Enterprise by gathering feedback and guidance from leaders, investigators, stakeholders, and peers. Contributes to implementing a clear roadmap aligned with surgical research priorities.

2. Develops and maintains collaborative relationships with investigators, clinical leaders, research staff, and partners. Builds an understanding of the clinical and research context and the strategic goals of the surgical divisions.

3. Cultivates external partnerships with professional associations, communities, universities, research institutes, government agencies, and solution providers or vendors to advance research and analytics objectives.

4. Collects and explores raw data from multiple sources to identify patterns, trends, and potential insights. Cleans, transforms, and validates data to ensure its quality and suitability for research and analysis.

5. Designs, develops, implements, and optimizes predictive and prescriptive models using statistical techniques and machine learning algorithms to improve accuracy and performance.

6. Identifies and engineers relevant features from datasets to strengthen model predictive power. Collaborates with clinical investigators and domain experts to extract meaningful features that improve model effectiveness.

7. Develops, evaluates, validates, and refines statistical and machine learning models to ensure accuracy, relevance, and effectiveness in clinical and research settings. Applies advanced analytical techniques to support clinically meaningful surgical research.

8. Creates compelling data visualizations and dashboards that communicate insights and findings effectively to technical and non-technical stakeholders using Tableau, Power BI, or custom code.

9. Prioritizes a limited number of high-impact research and analytics use cases. Collaborates with key partners and investigators to gather feedback, secure support, and make regular adjustments.

10. Identifies research opportunities and independently develops and leads data science and outcomes research projects from concept through dissemination, including research question development, study design, data identification, analysis, interpretation, and communication of findings.

11. Applies research and data science expertise and shares success stories and lessons learned with the Surgery Research Enterprise and broader research community. Teaches or coaches professionals in advanced analytics, data science, problem-solving methodologies, and related techniques to support professional development.

12. Monitors industry, healthcare, surgical research, and data science trends and best practices. Identifies opportunities to apply emerging methods to new research questions.

Other information:

Technical Expertise

  1. Strong organizational and problem-solving skills required, with an emphasis on attention to detail.
  2. Excellent written and oral communication skills, along with good interpersonal skills.
  3. Professional interaction with a diverse group of staff and users.
  4. Experience working independently and collaboratively with investigators and research teams to develop and execute research projects.
  5. Experience working with complex healthcare, clinical, research, or administrative datasets.
  6. Expert-level skills in research, data science, clinical and/or research decision-making processes, techniques, and tools (e.g., Snowflake, databricks, SAS, R, Python, SQL, etc.).
  7. Experience applying statistical techniques, machine learning, and advanced analytical methods to healthcare or clinical research data required.
  8. Demonstrated experience developing research questions, working with complex datasets, conducting advanced analyses, interpreting findings, and contributing to abstracts, presentations, manuscripts, or other scholarly products preferred.

Education and Experience

1. Education: Master's degree in data science, statistics, biostatistics, computer science, biomedical informatics, epidemiology, engineering, or a related quantitative field required. PhD or other relevant doctoral degree preferred.

2. Licensure: NA

3. Certification: NA

4. Years of relevant experience: Minimum of 3 years of relevant experience in data science, healthcare analytics, clinical research, outcomes research, or a related field required. Experience independently developing and leading research or analytical projects strongly preferred.

5. Years of supervisory experience: Preferred but not required.

Description Pricing is one of the most consequential decisions Amazon makes — and the science behind it needs to be causally rigorous, not just predictive. The P2 Optimization Science (P2OS) team builds the machine learning systems that power Amazon's pricing decisions at scale: demand lift models, customer lifetime value frameworks, and the experimentation infrastructure that validates whether our pricing changes actually work. We're hiring an Applied Scientist to own causal inference at the intersection of ML and pricing experimentation. This role exists because our team has identified a real gap: the methodological bridge between econometric analysis (owned by our economists) and production-scale ML pipelines (owned by our engineers) needs a practitioner who lives in both worlds. You'll build CATE estimation models, design analysis workflows for pricing weblabs, and develop the reusable causal ML infrastructure that the broader team — including non-ML scientists — can rely on. This is not a research role. The bias here is toward shipping production-quality causal pipelines with real downstream business impact. You'll measure success by what changes in LTV estimates, what pricing errors your models help avoid, and whether the economists on your team can actually use what you build. If you're a scientist who wants to work on hard causal identification problems in a high-stakes production environment — and who finds satisfaction in making rigorous methods accessible to a broader team — this role is for you. Description FBA Science seeks an Applied Scientist to invent and build optimization models and algorithms that improve how Amazon plans and places seller inventory across its worldwide fulfillment network. FBA moves the inventory of hundreds of thousands of sellers through a multi-echelon network of origin storage, national and regional distribution, and fulfillment centers — putting the right inventory in the right place, on time and at low cost. Operating this network is a constant stream of decisions: how much a seller should send, and where and when it should flow, all under scarce receiving and storage capacity. And these decisions are not ours to make alone — sellers choose what to send and how to respond to the options and incentives we offer, so we have to plan the network and shape seller behavior together. Solve it well and we drive out cost and speed up delivery, while making FBA the easiest way for a seller to grow their business. Our strategy is to make these decisions with science-driven technology, and because existing techniques rarely fit Amazon's scale and unique business needs, we invent new approaches and algorithms. As an Applied Scientist, you'll develop optimization models and algorithms across FBA's inventory planning and placement systems. Your role will initially focus on joint replenishment and placement decisions. Your models will impact business decisions worth billions of dollars and improve the experience of every FBA seller. Key job responsibilities - Own the development of the replenishment, placement, and transportation-planning algorithms that decide how a seller's inventory flows across Amazon's fulfillment network. - Design and implement large-scale optimization models and algorithms for complex inventory-planning problems, and the prediction and estimation layer they depend on. - Partner closely with Product Managers and engineers to define high-impact problems, translate ambiguous business challenges into well-scoped science initiatives, and deliver actionable, science-driven solutions. - Build and deploy science solutions into production pipelines, ensuring that models operate reliably at scale across a network serving hundreds of thousands of sellers. A day in the life You will own a science area with significant scope, impact, and high visibility, and your work will touch millions of products, hundreds of thousands of selling partners, and tens of millions of customers. You will be in the seller's critical path and you will be involved in every step, from idea generation and business analysis through research to the development and deployment of production-grade models. You will move between the optimization and the behavior. You are expected to make decisions about methodology, model architecture, and technology choices, and to strive for simplicity and demonstrate judgment backed by mathematical rigor. You will work closely with product managers, engineers, and fellow scientists, and collaborate with the broader science community across Amazon to broaden the horizon of your work. You will be entrepreneurial, wear many hats, and work in a fast-paced, high-energy, highly collaborative environment where we value people who deliver results, know their subject deeply, and are eager to learn new areas. About the team Sellers play a vital role in Amazon’s ecosystem, integral to our mission of offering the Earth’s largest selection, lowest prices, and fastest delivery speed. FBA is an optional service that enables third-party sellers to outsource order fulfillment to Amazon, and leverage Amazon’s world-class facilities to provide customers fast delivery promise. With commitment to taking on even more of the supply chain and operational complexities on behalf of our selling partners, Amazon now provides an end-to-end suite of supply chain services. This comprehensive solution empowers sellers to reliably transport products from manufacturing sites to customers worldwide. The FBA team is the core group in charge of warehousing, inventory management, fulfillment and pricing, and a diverse range of recommendation services for sellers, as well as building the internal resource management systems. We work to learn seller behavior, understand seller experience, recommend right actions to sellers, design seller policies and incentives, and develop science products and services that empower sellers to grow their businesses. To do so, we build and innovate science solutions that leverage the right tools across different fields including operations research, economics, machine learning, statistics, and data analytics. Our culture is centered on rapid prototyping, rigorous experimentation, and data-driven decision-making. Basic Qualifications - 2+ years of building models for business application experience - Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals - Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language - Demonstrated ability to build complex optimization models from scratch and take them to production. - PhD in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Economics, or a related quantitative field. Preferred Qualifications - Track record of translating ambiguous business problems into well-defined science solutions with measurable impact. - Proven ability to work effectively across product, engineering, and science teams. - Experience with supply chain optimization, demand forecasting, inventory management, or transportation/logistics algorithms. - Experience with reinforcement learning applied to sequential decision-making in operations or supply chain contexts. - Experience with product selection or assortment optimization for capacity-constrained systems. - Strength in mechanism design, auction theory, or game theory, particularly in settings involving strategic agents, capacity allocation, or market-based resource allocation.
